title: One idea into a week of content
summary: Turn one topic or source document into a draft outline, short posts and a review checklist.
free_route: Use the free tiers where available. Paste only material you own or are allowed to process; review every generated claim before publishing.
steps: Choose one topic and define the audience and goal.
Ask an AI assistant for a structured outline based only on the source notes you provide.
Request three short post drafts in distinct formats; label them as drafts.
Create visuals in a design tool or use a simple text-only template.
Fact-check, edit for your own voice, check image rights and schedule manually.
safety: Do not upload confidential client information. AI-generated claims and images need human review.

title: Build a research brief with sources
summary: Create a structured first-pass brief while keeping source links and separating facts from assumptions.
free_route: Start with public web sources and free access tiers. Verify important claims against the original source, not just an AI summary.
steps: Write one focused research question and define what is in and out of scope.
Use a search or answer engine to find primary sources and credible references.
Open the original sources and record the exact URLs, dates and relevant passages.
Ask an AI assistant to organise your notes into themes, evidence and open questions.
Check each factual statement against its source and mark anything uncertain.
safety: Never treat generated citations as verified. Do not use this workflow as the sole basis for legal, medical or financial decisions.

title: Sort incoming requests without auto-sending
summary: Use a simple form or spreadsheet plus human review to categorise incoming requests before replying.
free_route: Begin with a manual spreadsheet and copy/paste classification. Add an automation platform only after the process is stable; free limits vary.
steps: List the request categories and define what counts as urgent.
Create a spreadsheet with received date, category, owner, status and next action.
Remove personal or sensitive details before asking an AI assistant to classify sample requests.
Test the categories on a small batch and correct mistakes.
If automating later, route drafts to a human approval step; do not auto-send replies initially.
safety: Minimise personal data. Do not send sensitive messages or make consequential decisions solely from AI classifications.

title: Create a weekly progress report
summary: Turn your own task notes and metrics into a consistent weekly summary with decisions and next actions.
free_route: Keep a simple free spreadsheet and paste a cleaned summary into an AI assistant. No API key or integration is required.
steps: Collect completed tasks, blockers, key numbers and next-week priorities in one place.
Remove confidential details and check that figures are accurate.
Ask an AI assistant to organise the notes into wins, risks, decisions and next actions.
Compare the draft against the source notes and correct omissions or invented details.
Share the report yourself and assign owners to each action.
safety: Verify all numbers and names. Only share information with people authorised to see it.

title: Organise leads in a simple follow-up board
summary: Track enquiries and follow-ups in a spreadsheet first, with optional no-code automation after testing.
free_route: Start manually with a spreadsheet. If you later connect forms or email, check the provider's free limits and data-processing terms.
steps: Define the minimum fields you need: source, date, status, next action and owner.
Create a small board with clear statuses such as New, Contacted, Waiting and Closed.
Add only enquiries you have a lawful reason to store and a clear retention period for.
Test reminders manually before connecting an automation platform.
If automating, send notifications to the responsible person and keep human control over outreach.
safety: Follow applicable privacy and direct-marketing rules. Do not scrape contact details or send unsolicited bulk messages.

title: Use an AI coding assistant safely
summary: Use an assistant to understand a small code change, propose tests and explain a patch before you apply it.
free_route: Use documentation and free access tiers where available. For a small task, provide a minimal reproducible example rather than an entire private codebase.
steps: Describe one small bug or improvement and the expected behaviour.
Share only the relevant, non-secret code and ask for an explanation before a proposed change.
Ask for a minimal patch and tests covering normal and edge cases.
Review every line, run the tests and inspect dependencies before merging.
Keep a rollback path and never paste credentials, tokens or private keys into prompts.
safety: AI code can contain bugs or insecure patterns. Review dependencies, licences, secrets and security implications.
